data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism culminates in a non sequitur: after arguing that accepting 'smuggled induction' forces abandonment of a purely deductive science in favor of 'mitigated induction,' it suddenly concludes that 'the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all.' Nothing in the preceding reasoning establishes this. The entire argument is precisely about how the underlying epistemic structure (deductive justification vs. inductive support) determines the outcome for Popper's demarcation criterion. If the structure were 'never relevant,' the whole dispute between pure deduction and mitigated induction would be vacuous — yet the mechanism spends its substance arguing that the structure matters enough to force a revision of demarcation. The conclusion contradicts the argument's own load-bearing premise.
